A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MS-Temba, despite the changed title and substantial revision. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, references, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original MS-Temba results on TSU, MultiTHUMOS, and Charades, alongside component ablations, edge-device measurements, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v3 reports original results on TSU and Charades, new video-summarization results on SumMe and TVSum, revised ablations, and supplementary computational and qualitative evaluations.

M1.justification: v3 replaces v2's temporal convolutional modules with linear projections and separately parameterized dilated SSM branches. It adds projection-consistency loss, intermediate classification heads, auxiliary supervision, and a combined training objective. The summarization adaptation adds visual-text cross-attention and a regression head. The renamed MS-Fuser retains the earlier projection-sum-SSM fusion principle.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates action detection on TSU, MultiTHUMOS, and Charades. v3 removes MultiTHUMOS, retains TSU and Charades, and adds video summarization on SumMe and TVSum, substantially changing task and data coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the shared TAD Tables 1 and 2 is retained. New Table 7 introduces summarization comparisons with methods including dppLSTM, VASNet, CSTA, CLIP-It, A2Summ, and LLMVS, plus CLIP without MS-Temba. The separate edge-device comparison against a linear model and MS-TCT is removed.

E3.justification: The Charades training table changes batch size from 2 to 5 and epochs from 100 to 30; model size increases from 10M to 17M parameters. Summarization introduces sampled-frame importance prediction evaluated with Kendall's tau and Spearman's rho. v3 also resolves the stated Charades temporal-length discrepancy: v2's main text says 2000 while its appendix already says 256.

E4.justification: v3 adds loss-component and projection-alignment ablations, short-versus-long-action dilation analysis, and intermediate-block versus fused-output comparisons. Block-count and temporal-scaling studies remain with revised results. Directional-scanning, BiMamba-depth, feature-information-density, and video-duration analyses are removed. The TAD qualitative example is replaced, and a summarization case study is added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's action-duration standard deviations describe dataset variability, while v3's rank correlations are evaluation metrics; neither provides uncertainty estimates for model performance.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the earlier CLIP-based MS-Temba scores of 42.0/32.3 on TSU/Charades with 44.0/33.6; action-conditioned and ablation results also change. These concern a revised model and training settings, not controlled same-setting gains. New summarization results are 0.254/0.284 tau/rho on SumMe and 0.221/0.289 on TVSum. MultiTHUMOS and edge-device results disappear.

T1.justification: v3 introduces mathematical definitions for projection consistency, blockwise auxiliary supervision, and their combined objective, while removing v2's information-density definition. These are limited formal changes without new theorems or proofs. The standard SSM equations move from v2's appendix to v3's preliminaries and are not new theoretical content.

C1.justification: The headline contribution shifts from efficient, edge-deployable TAD with 10M parameters to broader long-video understanding with 17M parameters and state-of-the-art claims for TSU, Charades, and summarization. Explicit edge-training claims are dropped, efficiency claims are revised, and alignment plus auxiliary supervision replace convolutional local modeling in the principal method description.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations linking projection alignment to temporal coherence and auxiliary supervision to scale specialization, and interprets summarization results as evidence of broader applicability. It removes the information-density explanation and conclusions tied to several deleted analyses. The appendix discussion of VideoLLaVA and TimeChat limitations is retained rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: v3 specifies new loss weights, alpha=100 and beta=1, revises the architecture and training tables, and removes MultiTHUMOS and Jetson configuration details. The direct repository pointer becomes a project-page pointer. Backbone dimensions, principal TSU settings, and training GPU remain documented. Summarization training configurations promised in the text are absent from the supplied appendices.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds substantial positioning against visual and multimodal summarization research, including CSTA, CLIP-It, A2Summ, and LLMVS. Related work also adds end-to-end TAD, MOGO, and newer video/action-anticipation SSM work. This broadens the research positioning beyond v2's TAD-focused discussion; bibliographic updates to retained works are not counted as additions.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method narrative are extensively rewritten around ADL and supervised dilated branches. SSM preliminaries move into the main text, training receives a separate subsection, and summarization receives a full section. Appendices are reorganized into A-F, SSF is renamed MS-Fuser, and the title and author block change.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the introductory efficiency graphic and architecture diagrams, including a new branch-and-loss visualization. Block-count and temporal-scaling tables become plots, several earlier diagnostic figures disappear, and new loss and summarization tables are introduced. The supplementary qualitative displays and architecture table are substantially redesigned.

improvement.justification: v3 adds explicit method-specific ablations and evidence on a second task, but removes MultiTHUMOS and edge-device validation. Its new Table 4 reports inconsistent averages: 44.0 and 33.6 are summarized as 43.8 rather than 38.8, undermining the claimed average loss benefit. Summarization training details are also missing despite the appendix referral. These gains and reliability/reproducibility weaknesses prevent a confident net quality judgment.
